slides.say: Chord A B of a circle with center O is sixteen centimeters long. The distance from O to A B is six centimeters. What is the circumference of the circle, in centimeters?
at: Chord A B of a circle

slides.say: They ask for the circumference. That's the length all the way around the circle, the edge. It's a length, not the area inside.

Here's how we find it. If we go once around any circle, the length is a bit more than three times its diameter. That fixed number is called pi. It's the same for every circle, a little more than three. So the circumference is pi times the diameter.
at: That fixed number is called pi

slides.say: The diameter is two radii, two r. So the circumference is also two pi r. For example, a circle with diameter ten has a circumference of ten pi. A circle with radius three has diameter six, so its circumference is six pi. So really, they're asking for the radius.
at: So the circumference is also two pi r

slides.say: [short pause] Here's the figure again, bigger. We have a chord and its distance from the center, so one helper line will connect them.

[short pause] First, what is the distance from a point to a line? It's the shortest way, and that's the perpendicular. So from O we draw a line down to the chord, at ninety degrees. Call its foot M. O M is six.
at: So from O we draw a line

slides.say: We learned that a perpendicular from the center cuts the chord in half. Sixteen divided by two is eight, so A M is eight, and M B is eight.
Now the radius. We draw it from the center O to the end of the chord, B, so that it closes a triangle with the lines we already have. O B is a radius, so it's r.
at: We draw it from the center O

slides.say: [short pause] Look at triangle O M B. It has a right angle at M, its legs are six and eight, and the radius is its hypotenuse. Here it is, bigger.
at: Look at triangle O M B

slides.say: By Pythagoras, r squared is six squared plus eight squared. Six squared is thirty-six. Eight squared is sixty-four. Thirty-six plus sixty-four is one hundred, so r squared is one hundred.
A length is positive, so r is ten. You can also spot the triple. Six, eight, ten is three, four, five, doubled.
The circumference is two pi r, and r is ten. So it's two pi times ten, which is twenty pi. Choice number three is our answer.
at: The circumference is two pi r
So it's two pi times ten
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: In the exam you'd mark it and move on. Here, let's see where the other choices come from. One hundred pi is pi r squared. That's the formula for the area, the inside of the circle, and we'll learn it in the area lesson. This question asks for the length around, not the area inside.
at: One hundred pi is pi r

slides.say: Ten pi is what you get if you take ten as the diameter. And sixteen pi comes from taking the chord A B as a diameter. But this chord doesn't pass through the center, so it's not a diameter.
at: Ten pi is what you get

slides.say: Here's what to take from this question. When you're given a chord and its distance from the center, draw that distance and the radius to the end of the chord. Half the chord, the distance and the radius make a right triangle, and the radius is its hypotenuse. So any two of them give you the third. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Half the chord, the distance and the radius
